_meta.disclaimer: Compiled from public government sources for guidance only. Requirements can vary by state and change over time. Always verify current requirements with your nearest District Disability Rehabilitation Centre, Medical Board/CMO office, or the official portal before relying on this checklist.
sources: RPwD Act 2016, Schedule (list of 21 recognized disabilities)

process.cost: Free — no application fee, processing fee, or hidden costs.
steps: Register on the UDID portal (swavlambancard.gov.in) with your basic details.
Fill the online Disability Certificate + UDID application form and upload the required documents (offline/paper submission is also accepted at your district office and gets digitized later).
Your application is routed to a Medical Board / Chief Medical Officer (CMO) office, where specialists assess and certify your disability category and percentage.
Once certified, your Disability Certificate and UDID card are issued and can be downloaded/collected.
typical_documents: Aadhaar card (mandatory for UDID applications since the August 2023 notification)
Address proof (Aadhaar / Voter ID / utility bill)
Any existing medical records related to the condition, if available
process.note_on_percentage: A disability assessment of 40% or more is the threshold most commonly required to access statutory benefits, reservations, and concessions under the RPwD Act — but you can apply for a UDID/certificate at any assessed percentage; the Medical Board determines your actual percentage during assessment, not the applicant.

disability_categories.name: Hearing Impairment (Deaf and Hard of Hearing)
Multiple Disabilities Including Deaf-Blindness
typical_additional_docs: Assessment reports for each contributing condition

related_scheme_adip.name: ADIP (Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids and Appliances)
related_scheme_adip.note: Referenced as a next step after UDID — not part of MVP scope, shown for roadmap context only.
related_scheme_adip.eligibility: At least 40% disability (per UDID/certificate) and household income under ₹20,000/month.
